stories.title: The 0xFF02 extension commits T0; members install T0 and the TTL base from it
stories.description: Implements the `creation_timestamp_secs` field of the `0xFF02` SCP Context Parameters MLS group-context extension and validation rule 9, which `05-contexts.md` §5.13.3 (context creation) specifies. Alec chose this design on 2026-10-13. The creator's `ContextCreated` leaf timestamp (`T0`) is a genesis fact, so the creator commits it in the extension, and every member installs it from the committed extension as `T0` for the pseudonym rotation schedule (`09-security-model.md` §9.10.4.1) and as the TTL-deadline base (`05-contexts.md` §5.10). No member takes it from an invitation bundle signature, a snapshot field, or its own clock. The extension commits the value because a bundle signature proves only who signed the bundle (§5.12.3.1 step 4, §5.13.3 rule 8). A false `T0` would make a joiner rotate alone, so a relay could link its subscriptions across rotations, and it would move the joiner's TTL deadline. The field is required: SCP has no users, so no transition path accepts an extension without it. TTL extensions still reach a member as `TTLExtended` leaves in the event log, and ADR-049's single-source TTL-deadline invariant keeps the persisted `ContextSnapshot.creation_timestamp_secs` as the prune-immune base, now filled from the committed extension. PUSH-026, the pseudonym rotation runtime story, needs `T0` on a Welcome joiner, so this story blocks PUSH-026. The rotation runtime itself is PUSH-026, not this story. File locations are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: Creator writes the field (§5.13.3 'Creation timestamp'): a context created at test-clock time T0 carries a `0xFF02` extension whose JCS bytes include `creation_timestamp_secs` equal to the `timestamp` of the creator's `ContextCreated` leaf, and that value is unchanged in the extension after a later AddMember Commit. Creation rejects a creation timestamp above 2^53 − 1.

Install on join, import and restore (§5.13.3 rule 9): a Welcome joiner, an import and a restore each set the context's `T0` and its TTL-deadline base to the committed `creation_timestamp_secs`. A test whose invitation bundle, snapshot or local clock carries a different value shows the installed value still equals the committed one. The SDK rejects an import or restore whose snapshot creation timestamp differs from the committed value, before it installs any authority. Rule 9's keyless exception: an import or a restore of a snapshot that carries no MLS group installs no `T0`, arms no pseudonym-rotation schedule, and bases its TTL deadline on the creation timestamp the snapshot records (the exporter's value on an import, the member's own on a restore).

Reject a missing or invalid field (§5.13.3 rule 1 and rule 9): a Welcome join, an import and a restore each reject an MLS group whose `0xFF02` extension omits `creation_timestamp_secs`, carries a value above 2^53 − 1, or carries a value later than the member's clock plus 300 s, and each rejection installs no governance engine and no admin set. Rule 9's keyless exception: an import or a restore of a snapshot that carries no MLS group has no extension to check, so it applies none of these rejections and installs no `T0`.

Two-node test (§9.10.4.1 'Epoch schedule' and 'First v2 derivation'; §5.10 'Deadline base'): node A creates a context at T0 with `interval_secs` 3600 and a 5 h TTL, and node B joins through a Welcome at T0 + 3.5 h. B's first v2 epoch is 3, A and B each signal 'rotation due' at the same boundary T0 + 4 h, and B's TTL deadline is T0 + 5 h, not T0 + 8.5 h.

The two-node test above replaces the PUSH-026 test `a_welcome_joiner_admits_no_interval_rotation_without_the_creators_t0` in `spawn_from_welcome_tests.rs`, which the story deletes; a search of `crates/` for that test name returns no hit.
actionItems: Add the required `creation_timestamp_secs: u64` to the `0xFF02` extension type, its JCS serialization, and its validation, with the 2^53 − 1 bound.
Write the field at context creation from the `ContextCreated` leaf timestamp.
On Welcome join, import and restore, read `T0` and the TTL base from the committed extension, check the snapshot value against it, and apply the future bound of §9.8.2.
Replace the PUSH-026 Welcome-joiner test with the two-node test.

sources.section: ### 9. Persistence: coalesced by default, sync for safety-critical

details.missing: Two gaps stay open after this story, and other owners close them. (1) Spec 05 §5.13.3 rule 11, under which no Commit changes a genesis field of the `0xFF02` extension, has no enforcement: until SCP-338 (the story in which the `0xFF02` extension commits the TTL, the promotion policy, and the context mode) implements the genesis-field half of rule 11, a member can commit a changed `creation_timestamp_secs`, the other members merge that Commit, and a member that joins afterwards installs the changed value as `T0` and as its TTL base. (2) Rule 9 says a member that imported or restored a snapshot carrying no MLS group installs the committed `T0` when a Welcome gives it the group (the MLS group state reset of spec 23 §23.5). `Supervisor::spawn_actor_from_welcome` refuses a context for which the member holds a live actor or a durable snapshot, and a keyless import or restore leaves both, so that Welcome never installs. GitHub issue #3042, "a member holding a keyless snapshot cannot process the Welcome that would give it the group", owns this path.

stories.title: Derive the tier 3 push routing ID, bind bridge_target into the push preimages, and reserve the tier 3 ID on a bridged node
stories.description: Implements the tier 3 push routing ID that `09-security-model.md` §9.18.2 **Tier 3 push routing ID** defines, `SHA-256("scp-push-bridge:" || bridge_url || bridge_target)`, for an `SCPRelay` entry that carries a `bridgeTarget` (`18-addressability-and-deployment.md` §18.2.1). Alec chose the option in which "a relay entry becomes `{url, bridge_target}`" and the push routing ID is derived from the canonical URL plus the target. Before this story, `reserve_push_routing_id` in `crates/scp-node/src/published_state.rs` carried `// Stub — see PUSH-032` and left a bridged node's relay reserving its previous URL's ID, and `crates/scp-protocol/src/discovery/push.rs` computed only the `"scp-push-registration"` form; this story adds the tier 3 form beside it, so the code holds one derivation per form. The story also adds field 7 of the `PushRegistration` preimage and field 6 of the `PushDeregistration` preimage, `bridge_target`, 32 bare bytes holding the entry's target or `SHA-256(0x00)` (§9.5.2, `22-human-readable-addressing.md` §22.11.4), because `relay_url` alone is the bridge relay's URL and would let a message signed for the bridge relay, or for one node behind it, verify at every other node behind the same bridge. The separators stay `-V1:` (§9.5.2 note). `10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 relays** states each party's role: the bridged node reserves the tier 3 ID and does not reserve the bridge relay's own ID, the bridge relay computes nothing, and the client publishes inside `BRIDGE_DATA`. Delivery of a registration that arrives inside a forwarded `BRIDGE_DATA` is PUSH-033, which needs the node's bridge registration; this story covers the derivation, the preimages, the verifier, the shared relay URL handle and every listener. §10.7.1 **Tier 3 relays** has the node's relay open a **Tier 3 envelope** before it applies any rule to a PUBLISH at a reserved tier 3 ID, and PUSH-033 builds the opener, so until PUSH-033 lands a push-enabled relay rejects every PUBLISH at a reserved tier 3 ID with `4060` and stores nothing; it never verifies or stores an unsealed message there. A client that registers with a tier 3 relay is not in this story: a context's relay list cannot name a tier 3 relay's target, which `00-open-questions.md` records as open, and the client registrar stories take the new preimage field when they sign. Function names and file locations are indicators. The node's NAT tier yields one entry, the node's own, and an `IdentitySource::Explicit` document can carry further tier 3 entries with the node's `bridgeTarget`, which `insert_preferred_relay` and `set_preferred_relay` keep. The node reserves its own entry and every such entry of the document it is about to publish, at startup and on each tier change. Registering with several bridge relays at once would change the node's NAT handling, which this story does not cover.
acceptanceCriteria: Derivation (§9.18.2 'Tier 3 push routing ID'): one function in `scp-protocol` takes an `SCPRelay` entry (indicator: `relay_service_push_routing_id(&RelayService) -> [u8; 32]`) and returns `SHA-256("scp-push-bridge:" || canonical URL || 32 target bytes)` for an entry with a `bridgeTarget` and the existing `"scp-push-registration"` form for an entry without one. A unit test pins the bridge entry `wss://bridge.example.com/scp/v1` with target `f8affd47ab024cae9489a63fa1c632914c16f7329441b8fca65b32c78d86a4eb` to `733a76fce10004826ffaecd3c85ba27169282665cd64a902000275a52ba640a1`, and the direct entry with the same URL to `e47cce36c946ac50a2ee3dbc40f0416d7012bf82344c8f24a756c0f62242eea1`.

Non-collision (§9.18.2 'Why no tier 3 ID equals another push routing ID'): a test shows a bridge entry whose target is 32 printable ASCII bytes T has a tier 3 ID different from the `"scp-push-registration"` ID of the URL formed by the entry's URL followed by T; two bridge entries that differ only in target, and two that differ only in URL, have different IDs.

Relay URL handle carries the target: the relay's URL value (indicator: `RelayUrl` in `push_gate.rs`) built from a bridge entry holds the entry's canonical URL, its target and the tier 3 ID; built from a direct entry or from `RelayUrl::new(url)` it holds no target and the `"scp-push-registration"` ID. No conversion from an `SCPRelay` entry drops the target.

Preimage field (§9.5.2 field 7 of `PushRegistration`, field 6 of `PushDeregistration`): the signing-bytes functions take the target and append 32 bare bytes, `SHA-256(0x00)` = `6e340b9cffb37a989ca544e6bb780a2c78901d3fb33738768511a30617afa01d` when the relay has no target. The four existing goldens in `crates/scp-runtime/tests/test_vectors.rs` grow by 32 bytes each and end with the sentinel: `PUSH_REGISTER_A_HEX` from 193 to 225 bytes, `PUSH_REGISTER_B_HEX` from 200 to 232, `PUSH_DEREGISTER_A_HEX` from 127 to 159, and `PUSH_DEREGISTER_B_HEX` from 134 to 166. One new registration golden and one new deregistration golden end with the target above.

Verification (§10.7.1 step 3): `PushSignatureVerifier::verify` receives the target with the canonical URL, and the push handler verifies with the target of the entry the relay's handle holds for the PUBLISH's routing ID, never a value from the message. With the signature-checking test verifier, the push handler given the entry (bridge URL, target A) stores a registration signed for (bridge URL, target A), and rejects it with `4060` and stores nothing when given (bridge URL, target B) or the bridge URL with no target. A registration signed with the sentinel for the bridge URL is rejected with `4060` when the handler is given (bridge URL, target A). The same holds for a deregistration. The tests call the handler directly, because a push-enabled relay rejects every PUBLISH at a reserved tier 3 ID with `4060` until PUSH-033 opens the **Tier 3 envelope** (criterion 7).

Reservation replaces the stub (§10.7.1 'Tier 3 relays'): `reserve_push_routing_id` moves the shared handle to every tier 3 entry the node publishes, each with its own URL and target (a node MAY publish one entry per bridge relay, §10.12.4 'Multiple bridges'), so the relay reserves one tier 3 ID per entry, and `git grep -n "Stub — see PUSH-032" crates/` prints nothing. Both callers, the startup path in `crates/scp-node/src/lib.rs` and `apply_tier_change`, reach it with the entries the node publishes, before it publishes: the node's own entry and every `SCPRelay` entry of the document it is about to publish whose `bridgeTarget` is the node's. The node's own entry is always among them, so the reserved set cannot be empty and the reservation has no error.

Node behavior (§10.7.1 'Tier 3 relays'): a node test that changes the tier to a bridge entry shows a PUBLISH to the entry's tier 3 ID at the node's listener intercepted: the node's relay, which has no push selection before PUSH-012, answers `4063`, and a QUERY and a SUBSCRIBE at that ID afterwards return nothing. A PUBLISH to the bridge relay's own `"scp-push-registration"` ID is stored as an ordinary blob that a QUERY returns. The test that asserted the reserved ID stays in place on a change to a bridge entry, `tier_change_to_a_bridge_entry_publishes_it_and_keeps_the_reserved_id`, is rewritten to these assertions. A later change from the bridge entry back to a direct entry moves the reservation to the direct entry's `"scp-push-registration"` ID. Given two tier 3 entries with different bridge URLs and the same target, `reserve_push_routing_id` reserves both tier 3 IDs on the node's relay, and a PUBLISH at each is intercepted. A later reservation of one entry alone releases the other: its ID leaves the reserved set and joins the previous IDs the relay refuses without storing (PUSH-007). A node whose `IdentitySource::Explicit` document carries a second tier 3 entry with the node's `bridgeTarget` reserves both tier 3 IDs at startup and after a tier change. At the push gate, a push-enabled relay whose handle holds both entries rejects with `4060`, and stores nothing, a signed registration or deregistration presented without a **Tier 3 envelope** at either entry's ID, because §10.7.1 has the relay open the envelope first and the opener is PUSH-033. The push handler, given the entry the handle holds for an ID, verifies with that entry's URL and target: it accepts a registration signed for entry A when given A's entry and rejects it with `4060` when given B's entry, and once the handle holds A alone it holds no entry for B's ID, which the gate then refuses as a released ID. The same holds for a deregistration. A push-enabled node relay is PUSH-012. The Tier 3 envelope, which the node opens first for every PUBLISH at a reserved tier 3 ID on a listener or a bridge session (§10.7.1 'Tier 3 envelope'), is PUSH-033.

Every listener (WebSocket, QUIC, UDP/DTLS, WebTransport) intercepts the tier 3 ID once the handle holds a bridge entry, shown by one test per listener. A QUERY, and a SUBSCRIBE's backfill, at a current or released reserved ID returns no blob on every listener, including a blob stored before the ID became reserved (§10.7.1 **No blob storage**), shown by one test per listener; the UDP/DTLS listener takes no SUBSCRIBE, so its test covers QUERY.

Golden check (Python generator against Rust): `.docs/specs/25-test-vectors.md` §25.28 gains a vector (indicator: the next free vector number, after Vector 48) that prints the six push signing-bytes goldens above in hex, and the tier 3 vector of §9.18.2: bridge URL, target, the 79-byte preimage and the ID `733a76fce10004826ffaecd3c85ba27169282665cd64a902000275a52ba640a1`. `scripts/gen-test-vectors-p256.py` builds each of those values from its inputs and emits it, so `python3.12 scripts/check-test-vectors-p256.py`, which fails when a hex value spec 25 prints is missing from the generator output, compares the spec against an implementation independent of the Rust code. `test_vectors.rs` asserts the same hex against the Rust functions, and `cargo test -p scp-runtime --test test_vectors --features testing` passes. Before this criterion landed, spec 25 printed no push golden and the generator held no push code, so no check compared the push goldens with a second implementation.
actionItems: Add the tier 3 derivation beside `relay_endpoint_push_routing_id` in `crates/scp-protocol/src/discovery/push.rs`, with a constant for `scp-push-bridge:`, and one entry-taking function that selects the form from the entry.
Add the target to the relay URL value in `push_gate.rs` and to its conversion from `RelayService`.
Append the target to both signing-bytes functions and thread it through `PushMessage::signing_bytes`, `PushSignatureVerifier::verify`, `KelPushVerifier`, the test verifier and the push gate.
Replace the stub branch of `reserve_push_routing_id` and rewrite the node tests.
Regenerate the push goldens, add the tier 3 goldens and the spec 25 vector, and run the vector gate.

details.split: The story lands in two pull requests. The first carries acceptance criteria 1 to 5 and 9: the derivation, the non-collision tests, the relay URL handle, the preimage field, the verifier and push gate, and the spec 25 vector. The second carries criteria 6 to 8: the reservation that replaces the stub in `reserve_push_routing_id`, the node behavior, and the test per listener.

stories.title: A bridged node opens and handles a sealed push registration that arrives on a bridge session
stories.description: Implements the delivery half of `10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 relays** and the opening half of **Tier 3 envelope**: the registrant sends a PUBLISH frame whose payload is an HPKE envelope sealed to the wrapping key of the node's device, the device of the identity that publishes the tier 3 entry whose SCP instance runs the node, as a `BRIDGE_DATA` on a session the registrant opened to the node's `bridgeTarget`; the bridge relay carries it without parsing it (§10.12.4 **Sessions**); and the bridged node opens the envelope through that device's `KeyCustody` and applies every rule of §10.7.1 to the message inside, as it does for a PUBLISH on its own listener. A node MAY publish several tier 3 entries, one per bridge relay, and it reserves and opens per entry, with that entry's URL and target. SCP-340 serves each bridge session as a connection of the node relay's frame handling, so the node's answer returns on the session; no code in `scp-node` sends the `BRIDGE_REGISTER` that makes the bridge forward anything, which the linked issue in `blockedByIssues` tracks. PUSH-032 supplies the tier 3 ID, the preimage field and the reservation this story routes into. Until this story, the push gate's tier 3 arm (`gate_publish` in `crates/scp-transport/src/relay/push_gate.rs`, for a reservation whose entry carries a `bridgeTarget`) rejects every PUBLISH at a reserved tier 3 ID with `4060`; this story changes that arm to open the envelope with the matched entry and then run the push handler on the message inside. The tests that assert the rejection change with it: `enabled_rejects_an_unsealed_message_at_each_reserved_tier3_id_with_4060` in `push_gate.rs` and `enabled_relay_rejects_an_unsealed_registration_at_a_tier3_id_with_4060` in `crates/scp-transport/src/native/server.rs`, which then send a sealed message and expect the handler's answer, and keep an unsealed one as a malformed envelope (`4060`). The node answers a registration on a session with one of the three frames §10.7.1 **Tier 3 envelope** permits, `OK`, `4060` or `5000`, each with an empty `msg`, so the bridge relay learns accepted, rejected or ask again and nothing about the sealed message. The scp-protocol HPKE core (`crates/scp-protocol/src/crypto/hpke/p256.rs`, `open_with_external_dh`) already opens a Base-mode ciphertext from a Diffie-Hellman output computed in custody, which is the shape this story needs. File locations and type names are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: A PUBLISH at the node's reserved tier 3 push routing ID that arrives as a `BRIDGE_DATA` on a bridge session goes through the same push gate a listener PUBLISH goes through, after the envelope opens: with push enabled and the signature-checking test verifier, a registration signed for the bridge entry's URL and target and sealed to the node's device's wrapping key is stored in the node's registration store, and one signed for another target and sealed correctly is rejected and stores nothing.

An in-process test with a bridge relay whose broker role is enabled, a node registered with it, and a peer: the peer opens a session to the node's `bridgeTarget` and sends a `BRIDGE_DATA` carrying a PUBLISH whose payload is a sealed, signed `PushRegistration`, the peer receives a `BRIDGE_DATA` on the session carrying the node's `OK` with no `blob_id`, the node's store holds the registration, and the bridge relay's blob storage holds nothing at the tier 3 ID.

A session payload that does not decode as a relay frame gets, on that session, the `ERR` `4000` a listener connection gets for it, and the node's relay connection to the bridge relay and the session stay open.

Answers on a bridge session (§10.7.1 'Tier 3 envelope', **Opening, and what a failure does**): for a PUBLISH at a reserved tier 3 ID on a bridge session, the node sends exactly one frame in answer, carrying `OK` without `blob_id` when it accepts, `ERR` `4060` for every `4xxx` rejection and `ERR` `5000` for every `5xxx` rejection, each with an empty `msg`. One test per collapsed code drives a rejection the node would answer on a listener with `4061`, `4062`, `4063`, `4064`, `5003` and `5004` and asserts the bytes of the answer frame equal those of the `4060` frame (for `4xxx`) or the `5000` frame (for `5xxx`) apart from the echoed inner `ref`; the same messages on a listener connection get their own codes.

Envelope opening (`10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 envelope**): the node's relay validates `enc` (65 bytes, led by `0x04`, on the curve) before any Diffie-Hellman, computes the Diffie-Hellman output with `KeyCustody::dh_agree` on the identity's wrapping-key handle, opens `ct` with `info = "scp-push-bridge-seal-v1" || BE32(len(bridge_url)) || bridge_url || bridge_target` and `aad = BE32(len(bridge_url)) || bridge_url || bridge_target` built from the entry the PUBLISH arrived at, and strips the §9.10.3 bucket padding before it decodes. The same opening applies to a PUBLISH at the tier 3 ID that arrives on one of the node's own listeners.

Opener injection: the relay receives the envelope opener through its push configuration, beside the tier 3 reservation, as a trait object the relay crate defines and `scp-node` implements over the identity's `KeyCustody` (ADR-062, capability injection; indicator name: `PushEnvelopeOpener`). A node's reservation changes at runtime (`LiveRelayUrl::set`, called from the node's tier change), so a check against the reservation at construction is not enough: a push-enabled relay cannot be constructed without an opener, whatever its reservation is at construction, and the gate opens with that opener every PUBLISH at a tier 3 ID the handle holds when the PUBLISH arrives, including an ID reserved after construction. No global, singleton or `static` holds the opener or the key handle; `scripts/check-no-mutable-globals.sh` passes.

Misaddressed envelopes are rejected: five tests seal a correctly signed registration (a) with the `info` and `aad` of another bridge URL, (b) with those of another target, (c) to another identity's wrapping key (the §25.2 tertiary key where the node holds the secondary), (d) to the wrapping key of another device of the node's own identity, and (e) correctly for one tier 3 entry of a node that publishes two tier 3 entries with different bridge URLs and the same target (its own entry and a second one its `IdentitySource::Explicit` document carries with the node's `bridgeTarget`, PUSH-032), but delivered at the other entry's tier 3 ID. Each is rejected: the node's store and its stored timestamps are unchanged, the peer receives `ERR` `4060` with an empty `msg` on the session, and the same envelope sent on a listener connection gets `4060` PUSH_REGISTRATION_REJECTED. In case (e), the same node accepts an envelope sealed for each entry at that entry's own ID, which shows both entries are reserved and each opens with its own URL and target. After a tier change moves the node's own entry off its bridge relay, an envelope sealed correctly for that released entry and delivered at its ID is rejected with `4060`, and an envelope sealed for the document's second entry still opens.

Malformed envelopes are rejected with the same effects: a payload shorter than 65 + 16 + 256 bytes, a payload whose length minus 81 is not a §9.10.3 bucket size, a payload whose length minus 81 is the 256 KB bucket (above the tier 3 **Size ceiling**), an `enc` not led by `0x04` and one off the curve, a `ct` with one flipped bit, an opened plaintext whose length suffix exceeds the bytes before it, and an opened blob that does not decode. A test asserts `KeyCustody::dh_agree` is never called for the invalid `enc` cases.

Stored form: after an envelope opens and the registration is accepted, the node's registration store holds the decoded registration and no byte of the envelope; a test reads the store row and asserts it equals the row a direct listener registration of the same message produces.

The bridge relay cannot read the payload: in the in-process test, the bytes the bridge relay receives in the `BRIDGE_DATA` contain neither the registrant's 32 identifier bytes nor its `scp:` text form, nor the token, nor any listed routing ID, nor the 8-byte timestamp; and two registrations from one device that list different numbers of routing IDs but whose blobs fill the same §9.10.3 bucket (indicator: an APNs token with one and with two routing IDs; the test asserts both blobs fall in one bucket before it compares) produce `BRIDGE_DATA` payloads of equal length. The `BRIDGE_DATA` bytes the bridge relay receives from the node for an accepted registration and for one rejected with each code of the previous criterion contain none of those values either.

Envelope vector (`10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 envelope**; `.docs/specs/25-test-vectors.md`): spec 25 gains a vector (indicator: in §25.12, the HPKE vectors, as the next free vector number) with fixed inputs: recipient key the §25.2 secondary key, ephemeral private scalar the §25.2 tertiary private scalar, bridge URL `wss://bridge.example.com/scp/v1`, target `f8affd47ab024cae9489a63fa1c632914c16f7329441b8fca65b32c78d86a4eb`, and blob the 32 ASCII bytes `scp tier 3 push envelope vector!`. It prints `info`, `aad`, the 256-byte padded plaintext, `enc` and the 337-byte payload in hex. `scripts/gen-test-vectors-p256.py` gains the RFC 9180 Base-mode `SetupBaseS` with a fixed ephemeral scalar for DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 and AES-128-GCM, builds each printed value from those inputs and emits it, so `python3.12 scripts/check-test-vectors-p256.py` passes. `crates/scp-runtime/tests/test_vectors.rs` asserts `info` and `aad` against the Rust builders and opens the printed payload with the secondary private scalar to the printed padded plaintext and the blob. The vector is printed in the same change that adds the generator code, because the gate fails on a printed hex value the generator does not emit; the generator holds no HPKE seal today.

stories.title: A bridge relay rejects a PUBLISH at the tier 3 push routing ID of a node it brokers
stories.description: Implements **Misdirected registrations** in `10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 relays**. A client that sends a tier 3 registration to the bridge relay directly, instead of inside `BRIDGE_DATA`, would otherwise have the bridge relay store the plaintext registration as a blob and deliver the identity's token to any subscriber of that routing ID. The bridge relay already holds both inputs of the tier 3 push routing ID, its own canonical URL and each routing ID registered through `BRIDGE_REGISTER` (§10.12.4), so it computes each ID with PUSH-032's derivation and rejects a PUBLISH at it with `4060` PUSH_REGISTRATION_REJECTED (ADR-004), without verifying a signature. The rule is defense in depth under the relay tenet: the bridge relay is untrusted, and no client relies on it. This story owns bridge-relay PUBLISH handling; the node side is PUSH-032 and PUSH-033. File locations are indicators.
acceptanceCriteria: A relay whose broker role is enabled and which holds a `BRIDGE_REGISTER` registration for target T rejects a PUBLISH at `SHA-256("scp-push-bridge:" || its own canonical URL || T)` with `4060`, whatever the push role, and a QUERY and a SUBSCRIBE at that ID afterwards return nothing.
After the registration for T ends (the registrant disconnects), a PUBLISH at that ID is stored as an ordinary blob, so the rule covers only targets the relay currently holds.
A PUBLISH at the tier 3 ID built from another URL with T, or from the relay's own URL with a target it holds no registration for, is stored as an ordinary blob.
A relay holding registrations for two targets rejects a PUBLISH at the tier 3 ID of each with `4060`.
actionItems: Keep the set of tier 3 push routing IDs of held targets beside the bridge registry, updated on register and deregister.
Reject a PUBLISH at an ID in that set with `4060` before storage, in the same gate the reserved push routing ID passes through.
Add the tests to the native server's push tests.

stories.title: The client seals a tier 3 push registration to the publishing identity and sends it on a bridge session
stories.description: Implements the registrant client's role in `10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 relays**: for a relay held as an `SCPRelay` entry that carries a `bridgeTarget` (`18-addressability-and-deployment.md` §18.2.1), the registrar computes the entry's tier 3 push routing ID (`09-security-model.md` §9.18.2), signs over the entry's canonical URL and target (§9.5.2), and sends the PUBLISH frame on a session it opens through the bridge relay to the target (§10.12.4 **Sessions**), never as a direct PUBLISH to the bridge relay. The story cannot start until the first open question in `00-open-questions.md`, how a context's relay list names a tier 3 relay, is decided, because the registrar learns its relays from the contexts it belongs to and that list carries no target today; the linked issue in `blockedByIssues` tracks the decision, since `blockedBy` names stories only. The registrar itself is PUSH-014 and the derivation is PUSH-032. File locations are indicators. The client also seals each tier 3 message in the `10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Tier 3 envelope**: it takes `pkR` from the tier 3 entry's `wrappingKey` (`18-addressability-and-deployment.md` §18.2.1 **`wrappingKey`**), which names the wrapping-key entry of the node's device, checks that the identity's key state lists that key `Current` as a device's wrapping-key entry (§10.7.1 **Recipient key**), and seals the signed, padded message to it, so the bridge relay forwards ciphertext. The client reads no KeyPackage to learn `pkR`. A reader accepts `wrappingKey` only when its 33 bytes equal the `key` of a wrapping-key entry the identity's resolved `KeyState` lists `Current`, and the device of that entry is the node's device; when the bytes match no `Current` wrapping-key entry, it treats the tier 3 entry as absent and never acts on the record's bytes alone (`03-identity.md` §3.10.13). The keri workstream owns the wrapping-key entry, and keri P7 (#2874) re-signs the service record after a wrapping-key rotation. That check reads the per-device wrapping-key role keri P7 adds to the key state (`09-security-model.md` §9.7.4.2), which the second issue in `blockedByIssues` tracks. SCP-346, the story in which a node names its device's wrapping-key entry in each tier 3 entry it publishes, writes the field this story reads. It reads the node's `OK`, `4060` or `5000` on the session. A tier 3 message's blob is at most 65,532 bytes (**Size ceiling**).
acceptanceCriteria: For a tier 3 entry, `register` publishes to the entry's tier 3 push routing ID and signs a preimage ending with the entry's canonical URL and `bridgeTarget`; a test checks both against PUSH-032's derivation.

The registrar sends that PUBLISH only as a `BRIDGE_DATA` on a session it opened with a `BRIDGE_SESSION_OPEN` whose `target_routing_id` is the entry's `bridgeTarget`, and the PUBLISH payload is the sealed envelope, never the plain message; a test with a recording relay connection shows no direct PUBLISH at the tier 3 ID and no `BRIDGE_DATA` payload that decodes as a `PushRegistration`.
`deregister` for a tier 3 entry follows the same route and signs the same target.

An in-process test with a bridge relay and a bridged node stores the registration in the node's store and nothing in the bridge relay's blob storage, and `register` returns success only after the node's `OK` arrives on the session. With the node made to reject (a registration signed for another target), `register` returns a typed rejection from the node's `4060`; with the node made to answer `5000`, a typed retryable error; and with the session closed before the answer arrives (a test bridge that sends `BRIDGE_SESSION_CLOSE` after it carries the PUBLISH), a typed error stating that the outcome is unknown, after which the next `register` signs a newer `timestamp` and the node stores it; and with the client's connection to the bridge relay dropped after the bridge carries the PUBLISH and before the answer (`10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **The registrant client**), the same typed outcome-unknown error, after which the next `register`, on a new connection and session, signs a `timestamp` newer than the first attempt's and the node stores it.

Recipient key (`10-infrastructure-and-self-hosting.md` §10.7.1 **Recipient key**, `18-addressability-and-deployment.md` §18.2.1 **`wrappingKey`**): for a tier 3 entry whose `wrappingKey` names K1, a key the identity's key state lists `Current` as a device's wrapping-key entry, the client seals to the 65-byte uncompressed SEC1 form of K1, and a recording bridge connection shows no `QUERY` at the identity's KeyPackage routing ID (`09-security-model.md` §9.7.4 **KeyPackage routing ID**) before the registration's `BRIDGE_DATA`.

Recipient key refusals (§10.7.1 **Recipient key**): the client refuses to seal, with a typed error and no `BRIDGE_DATA`, in each of these cases, one test per case: the entry carries no `wrappingKey`; the key state lists the named key `Superseded`; the key state lists the named key `Compromised{from: N}`; the key state lists the named key only in an entry that is not a wrapping-key entry (the identity's `#active` key); the key state does not list the named key; and the named 33 bytes do not decompress to a point on the P-256 curve (indicators: `Tier3WrappingKeyAbsent`, `Tier3WrappingKeyNotCurrent`, `Tier3WrappingKeyInvalid`).

Resolution freshness (§10.7.1 **Recipient key**, `09-security-model.md` §9.10.4 **Superseded wrapping key**): under an injected clock and a recording resolver, the client refuses to seal, with a typed error and no `BRIDGE_DATA`, in each of these cases, one test per case: its resolution of the identity's service record fails; its resolution of the identity's key state fails; the service record it holds is older than `MAX_ATTESTATION_KEY_RESOLUTION_STALENESS` (300 seconds, `09-security-model.md` §9.18.7) and the resolution it makes again fails; and the key state it holds is older than that bound and the resolution it makes again fails. With both held copies resolved exactly 300 seconds before the clock, the client seals without resolving again; with either held copy resolved 301 seconds before the clock and a working resolver, the client resolves that copy again before it seals, and the recording resolver shows that resolution before the `BRIDGE_DATA`.

Sealing: the client pads the message's blob under §9.10.3, seals it in HPKE Base mode under the §9.5 suite to `pkR` with `info = "scp-push-bridge-seal-v1" || BE32(len(bridge_url)) || bridge_url || bridge_target` and the matching `aad` built from the entry, and frames the payload as `enc || ct`; a test opens the recorded payload with the recipient's private key and recovers the signed message byte for byte, and checks the payload length is 65 + bucket + 16.

A ciphertext addressed to another node or target is rejected: in the in-process test, an envelope the client seals for entry A and that is delivered to the node at entry B (another `bridgeTarget`, and separately another bridge URL) stores nothing in the node's store; an envelope sealed to a second identity's wrapping key and delivered to the first identity's node stores nothing.

The bridge relay cannot read the payload: in the in-process test, the `BRIDGE_DATA` bytes the bridge relay receives from the client contain neither the registrant's identifier in raw or `scp:` form, nor the token, nor any listed routing ID.

Current wrapping key (§10.7.1 **Recipient key**, **Current wrapping key**): after the node's device rotates its wrapping key from K1 to K2, so the key state lists K2 `Current` and K1 `Superseded`, and the service record is re-signed naming K2 on the tier 3 entry (keri P7 (#2874)), the client's next `register` and `deregister` each resolve the identity's service record and key state again and seal to K2, and a test shows the node, holding only K2, stores the registration. A client that resolves the old entry naming K1 together with the new key state refuses to seal with the typed not-current error and sends no `BRIDGE_DATA`.

Size ceiling (§10.7.1 **Size ceiling**): a registration whose blob is 65,532 bytes is sealed in the 64 KB bucket and sent, with a payload of 65,617 bytes; one whose blob is 65,533 bytes is refused before any `BRIDGE_DATA`, with a typed error (indicator: `Tier3RegistrationTooLarge`) that names the ceiling; and a bridge relay configured with a `max_blob_size` below the `BRIDGE_DATA` that carries a 64 KB-bucket envelope closes the session with `BRIDGE_SESSION_CLOSE` `4010`, which `register` returns as the bridge relay's typed refusal.

stories.title: Registrar signs with the device's P-256 `#active` key
stories.description: §10.7.1 step 3 and §22.11.4 have the registrant sign a push message with the P-256 key its key state lists `Current` in the `#active` role. The device's `#active` key is Ed25519 until SCP-315 moves it to P-256, so PUSH-014 ships its registrar with a `PushSigningKey` that only `testing` can build. This story adds the production constructor, which takes the custody handle the device's key state lists `Current` in `#active` and no other handle, and proves the two criteria that need that key. PUSH-015's `push_enable` is the first production caller.
acceptanceCriteria: `PushSigningKey` has a constructor outside `testing` that takes the custody handle the device's key state lists `Current` in the `#active` role, and it refuses any other handle.

Against a relay wired with the signature-checking test verifier of PUSH-005, which checks a real P-256 signature against a key the test supplies and compiles only under `testing` and the device's `#active` public key, `register` stores one registration per relay.

`register` signs one message per relay, each over that relay's canonical URL; a test with two relays shows that the two signed preimages differ and that each relay rejects the other relay's message with 4060.
actionItems: Add the production `PushSigningKey` constructor from the key state's `#active` handle.
Prove the two relay criteria with the device's `#active` key.
